title: Right-Wing Strategic Litigation in Times of Culture Wars Before the ECtHR
discipline: International and Comparative Human Rights Law
summary: How conservative and religious groups are using the European Court of Human Rights to push back against gender equality, LGBTI+ rights, and other progressive norms — and why this makes the Court a contested arena rather than a neutral one.

title: The Constitutional Role of Municipalities in the Governance of Social Rights: A Comparative Study of Turin, Barcelona, and Athens
discipline: International and Comparative Human Rights Law
summary: A comparative study of Barcelona, Turin, and Athens on how cities handle the rights to education, health, and housing — finding that local innovation matters, but cannot substitute for clear legal powers and stable financing.

title: Navigating the City: Internal Migration of Refugees from Dadaab and Kakuma Refugee Camps to Nairobi, Kenya
summary: Across Kenya, many refugees are choosing to leave camps and move to cities as a deliberate strategy for survival, dignity, and opportunity. This research argues that policy needs to catch up with that lived reality instead of treating it as irregular.

title: Case Note: Mariam Sajjad v. Prof. Dr. Rasool Ahmed Chaudhary (Lahore High Court, 2023)
institution: Pakistan International Law College Jauharabad (affiliated with University of the Punjab, Lahore)
summary: A case note on a 2023 Lahore High Court medical negligence ruling, examining when a doctor's conduct crosses the line into a violation of a patient's right to life and dignity.

title: Court Administration and Judicial Independence: Beyond the Judge, the Court Registrar in Cameroon
summary: How institutional weaknesses in Cameroon's court registries — unclear hierarchies, weak implementation, thin administrative support — shape litigants' access to justice and quietly undermine judicial independence, long before a case ever reaches a judge.
